title: Localized Cutaneous Versus Deep Sporotrichosis at Hospital das Clínicas, UFMG, Belo Horizonte, Brazil: A Cohort of 213 Culture-Confirmed Cases, 2011 to 2026
content: Background: The zoonotic epidemic of sporotrichosis caused by Sporothrix brasiliensis has expanded throughout Brazil and other countries, with a rise in deep forms of disease. Detailed comparative data on presentation, treatment and outcome of cutaneous and deep disease are needed to follow how Brazilian cohorts are evolving. Methods: Retrospective observational cohort of patients with sporotrichosis treated at a quaternary university hospital in Belo Horizonte between 2011 and 2026, restricted to culture-positive cases. Localized cutaneous disease was compared with deep infection using logistic regression adjusted for age and sex. Results: Of 313 patients, 213 had a positive culture. Median age was 41 years and 54.0% were women. Lymphocutaneous disease predominated (54.0%) and contact with cats was reported by 53.1%. Median treatment duration was 150 days. Among the 101 patients with a defined outcome, 97 were cured (96.0%), with no documented treatment failure. All four sporotrichosis-related deaths occurred in the deep infection group, which was independently associated with comorbidity (OR 9.69; 95% CI 2.52 to 37.23) and with an immunosuppressive condition (OR 6.61; 95% CI 1.89 to 23.09). Conclusions: Localized cutaneous sporotrichosis was cured in nearly all patients with documented follow-up, whereas mortality was confined to deep infection associated with comorbidity and immunosuppression.
